messages:
olga: Heads-up: onboarding kepler-14b-int3 to the long-context suite — seeing KV snapshot loss once sequences exceed ~65k tokens during a warm-restart + shard crossover. Repro below.
aj: :eyes: Can you paste the minimal repro and which quant profile you used?
olga: Test harness: `longroll-v2` on dev-gpu-14. Steps:
```
1) load model kepler-14b-int3 (quant-profile: q3-fast) with shard A
2) prefill with 70k token document (synthetic, 2x paragraphs repeated)
3) trigger shard swap to B (simulate node upgrade)
4) continue generation -> observe km_loss / repeated tokens
```
Logs:
```
[2026-03-20T14:12:08Z] prefill done, kv_size=70_213
[2026-03-20T14:12:09Z] checkpoint snap saved: snap-20260320-141209
[2026-03-20T14:12:12Z] restore snap-20260320-141209 -> kv_size=0  <-- uh
[2026-03-20T14:12:13Z] generated tokens start repeating
```
olga: Note: same test on fp16 baseline (kepler-14b-fp16) passes fine, kv_size preserved.
kevin: Interesting — could be int3 pointer packing rounding the kv index. Did you try forcing `rot_scale=1.0` vs `rot_scale=0.9998`?
olga: Yep. When we set `rot_scale=1.0` the divergence still happens but later (~72k). With `rot_scale=0.9998` it's at ~63k. Hypothesis: combined effect of quantized kv offsets + RoPE scaling causing misalignment during snapshot serialization.
maya: Any diffs in snapshot file size or checksum between q3 and fp16?
olga: q3 snapshot is ~124MB, fp16 ~392MB. Checksums show mismatch at byte offset ~1_048_576 (the first MB boundary) across multiple runs.
zack: Could also be struct packing on the restore path — we had a bug where int-packed KV segments weren't aligned on 64B boundaries after memcpy for certain GPUs. Remember the `cuda_memcpy_aligned` fix we made last quarter.
aj: Can you try a reproduce that logs per-shard kv_index hashes before save and after restore? Maybe include the `kv_index_root` we compute in runtime.
olga: Added diff logging, attaching snippet: 
```
# kv index root check
before_save: hash=0x7a1d19f3, entries=10921
after_restore: hash=0x00000000, entries=0
```
ci-bot: longroll-v2 pipeline triggered: https://ci.internal/longroll-v2/3712 :white_check_mark:
kevin: Two quick experiments to try:
- force `serialize_kv_as_bigendian=false` (we had an endian switch in q3 serializer)
- run snapshot/restore with `--no-compress` to rule out mis-tuned LZ4 compressor on small blocks
maya: Also run with `--kv-padding=64` to ensure alignment and see if checksum changes.
olga: Running three forks now, will post logs. Initial quick numbers: fp16 run completed snapshot+restore with KV preserved at 70k; int3 w/ no-compress still zeros the kv on restore; int3 w/ padding=64 preserves but generation has slight drift (perplexity +2.3%).
zack: That's telling — padding helps, so allocator/packing issue likely.
aj: Should you block kepler-14b-int3 on Dedicated until we trace root cause? Product might want it live for perf.
maya: From perf POV int3 gives 1.3x token throughput (85ms/1k vs 110ms/1k) but regressions on longprefill are unacceptable for some customers.
olga: Filing an internal bug: INF-7129 and marking as P1 for onboarding. Adding reproduction artifacts to the ticket.
kevin: Short term mitigations: disable snapshotting for models with quant-profile=q3-fast OR force `kv-padding=64` and `serialize_kv_as_bigendian=false` in the int3 serializer.
zack: Agree. Also add a regression test to longroll-v2: prefill 80k tokens + snapshot/restore + compare kv_index hash exact match.
olga: Will add test and a unit that fuzzes different rot_scale values. Thanks all. I'll update INF-7129 with links and results. :thumbsup:
